submission.justification: Sensor-T2 has the best unirradiated resolution (6.0 um), but after 2e16 neq/cm^2 its hit efficiency is only 82.0%. That is far below the >=97% end-of-life requirement for the innermost layer: charge trapping is strong and full depletion can no longer be reached. So T2 is ruled out. Of the two candidates that pass, Sensor-T1 (planar) has 98.5% efficiency and 9.0 um resolution. Sensor-T3 (3D) has 99.2% efficiency but worse resolution (14.0 um) because of its larger pitch. T1 therefore gives the best resolution that meets the radiation constraint. I chose 150 um because it is the only thickness with simulated resolution data (2025 summary, 150 um). I had no tool to check how resolution changes with thickness, so I did not optimise thickness. Caveats: the resolution numbers come from unirradiated simulation, so the ranking after irradiation is not confirmed. The irradiation report also does not say what thickness was tested.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible single-hit spatial resolution in innermost layer
requirements.evidence: T1 has 9.0 um at 150 um (2025 sim, unirradiated), the best among candidates that meet the radiation requirement. T2 (6.0 um) fails on radiation. T3 is 14.0 um. Resolution after irradiation and the effect of thickness were not simulated.
